note: The lane ruled `uses` out on prose ("member access on structs is a field read — no edge, fields already have contains ownership") with no corpus measurement, while six lanes publish exactly this edge for the same construct and ERLANG — Elixir's nearest neighbour, whose records are Elixir's structs — publishes it as `uses -> <field>`. Measured: 2,157 live member reads in 177 of 568 corpus files, 1,009 of which name a field some struct in the corpus declares. The gate is a DECLARED field of the same file AND (EX-EX12) a receiver that is not bound to a MAP in the enclosing definition; four silences are pinned because each is where a guessed target could have been published: a map-key read (`opts.domain`) is the same syntax with no type information behind it, a method call is a CALL not a read, a CAPITALIZED receiver is a module reference not a field read, and a chained read takes the LEAF. `@doc`-style `contains` ownership is not a substitute for the read edge — it says who owns the field, not who reads it. `meta.evidenceClass` is pinned on the read edge for the same reason as the exports fixture.

expectRelationships.note: a CHAIN publishes its leaf — `u.profile.name` reads `name`
EX-EX12: `%Mod{} = u` binds a STRUCT, so the read through it IS a struct-field read — the map gate must not swallow it

forbidRelationships.note: a MAP KEY read: no declared struct field named domain

EX-EX12: the receiver is bound by `%{} = m`, so `m.id` is a MAP KEY read. `id` IS a declared struct field of this file, which is exactly why the declared-field gate alone published this edge — the corpus case is `defp from_map(%{} = datetime_map)` reading eleven map keys in calendar/datetime.ex:2063
a CALL is a calls edge, not a read
a capitalized receiver is a module reference
a chain publishes its LEAF (`name`), and `profile` is not a declared field here
R7: a struct-literal receiver is a VALUE, and a target carrying `%`/`{}` names no symbol
